title: Khao Niao Mamuang
subtitle: sweet sticky rice and mango dessert with salted coconut cream
excerpt: Thailand's iconic sticky rice dessert with ripe mango and a salted coconut topping. Serves four.
sourceNotes: Khao niao mamuang is one of the most iconic Thai desserts, sold throughout Thailand especially during mango season.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Season the rice up to 2 hours ahead at room temperature. Slice the mango just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: Also called sticky rice or sweet rice. A short-grain rice that must be soaked before steaming. It becomes dense and chewy when cooked.
Full-fat coconut milk is used to season the rice and make the salted topping cream.
Natural sweetener from palm sap. Its mild caramel flavour suits this dessert particularly well.
Used in the salted coconut topping to give a clean sweetness.

content.text: Khao niao mamuang serves 4 and takes about 45 minutes plus soaking time.
Glutinous rice
is soaked overnight, steamed until tender, then seasoned with sweetened
coconut milk
and
palm sugar
. The salted coconut topping uses
caster sugar
and a generous pinch of salt. Serve alongside 2 ripe mangoes, sliced (no ingredient slug; slice the mango fresh just before plating).
The salted coconut topping should taste noticeably salty-sweet, not just sweet. The salt is what makes it work against the mango and rice.
What you need
Method
Drain the soaked glutinous rice. Steam in a lined steamer basket over boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes until the grains are tender and translucent throughout.
While the rice steams, heat 250 ml coconut milk with the palm sugar and a pinch of salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until dissolved. Do not boil.
Transfer the hot rice to a large bowl. Pour the warm sweetened coconut milk over it and stir gently. Cover and leave for 15 minutes to absorb. The rice will become glossy and dense.
Make the topping. Heat 150 ml coconut milk with the {{caster-sugar}} and a generous pinch of salt over medium heat until just warmed and dissolved. The topping should taste salty-sweet.
Peel 2 ripe mangoes and slice the flesh away from the stone. Arrange on plates alongside a mound of the sticky rice.
Spoon the warm salted coconut topping over the rice. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Rice is too dry and not absorbing the coconut milk
items.cause: Rice was not hot enough when the coconut milk was poured over
items.fix: Always season the rice immediately off the steamer while it is still very hot.

items.cause: Not enough salt in the topping
items.fix: Add more salt in small pinches until the salty note is clearly present before the sweet one.

items.cause: Too much coconut milk absorbed or rice over-soaked
items.fix: Reduce the seasoning coconut milk to 200 ml next time. Use rice soaked no longer than 8 hours.

content.text: Where this dish lives

Khao niao mamuang is Thailand's most celebrated dessert outside the country. Market stalls pack it into individual portions wrapped in banana leaf or plastic film for people to eat as they walk. The dish is tied to the mango season. Thais are particular about the mango variety: firm, sweet, and only slightly fibrous is the ideal. The salted coconut topping is not an afterthought. It is the contrast between that salt and the sweet rice and fruit that makes the dish so compelling.
